title: Constant-path comparison for a Kan-fibration pullback
statement:
Use the simplicial sets, quasicategories, spaces and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in its fixed universe convention. Let $u:U\to W$ and $v:V\to W$ be maps of Kan complexes. Define
$$P(u,v)=U\times_{W,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,W}V,$$
where $\operatorname{ev}_e$ restricts a simplicial path to its endpoint $e$. This is a Kan complex. If either $u$ or $v$ is a Kan fibration (right lifting property against all horn inclusions $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0\leq k\leq n$), then the map $U\times_W V\to P(u,v)$ that inserts the constant path at the common image is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 3.4.0.7 (0329), with path model Construction 3.4.0.3 (010B). The path model is Kan since endpoint evaluation to W × W is a Kan fibration by Corollary 3.1.3.3 (00TM) and its base is U × V. Read online 2026-10-16, not archived in literature/. Kerodon tags, unrelated to Stacks 0329.

proof.text: Put $I=\Delta^1$ and $T=\operatorname{Fun}(I,W)$, using the degreewise internal functor and product definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. We first prove that $(\operatorname{ev}_0,\operatorname{ev}_1):T\to W\times W$ is a Kan fibration. A horn lifting problem for this map is exactly a map to $W$ from $(I\times\Lambda_k^n)\cup_{\partial I\times\Lambda_k^n}(\partial I\times\Delta^n)$, to be extended to $I\times\Delta^n$: the two prescribed endpoints give the map on $\partial I\times\Delta^n$, and the given horn of paths gives the other part. The inclusion is the pushout-product of the monomorphism $\partial I\hookrightarrow I$ and the horn inclusion $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. A horn inclusion is anodyne by the definition of Kan fibration: every Kan fibration lifts against it. The pushout-product is therefore anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product], and $W\to\Delta^0$ is a Kan fibration since $W$ is Kan, so the extension exists. The displayed $P(u,v)$ is the pullback of this endpoint-pair map along $(u,v):U\times V\to W\times W$. For a horn in $P(u,v)$, fill its $U$ and $V$ coordinates separately, using their Kan conditions, then solve the endpoint-pair lifting problem with these prescribed coordinate fillers. The resulting triple is a filler in $P(u,v)$. This proves its Kan assertion without any fibration hypothesis on $u$ or $v$.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.3; Construction 3.4.0.3 (010B). The lifting argument is expanded using the existing anodyne pushout-product statement.

proof.text: For either $e\in\{0,1\}$, prove that $\operatorname{ev}_e:T\to W$ lifts against every $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, including $m=0$. Under the same internal-functor definition, a lifting problem prescribes a map to $W$ on $(\partial\Delta^m\times I)\cup_{\partial\Delta^m\times\{e\}}(\Delta^m\times\{e\})$. The inclusion into $\Delta^m\times I$ is the pushout-product of the monomorphism $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ and $\{e\}\hookrightarrow I$. Each endpoint inclusion is a one-dimensional horn inclusion and hence anodyne. By [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] this union inclusion is anodyne, so the Kan condition on $W$ supplies the extension. In dimension zero this is just extension from the chosen endpoint of $I$; no nonemptiness assumption on $W$ is used. The boundary-lifting characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] now says that both endpoint evaluations are trivial fibrations, hence weak homotopy equivalences. Moreover a pullback of either evaluation still has boundary lifting: project a boundary lifting problem to $T\to W$, choose its filler there, and pair it with the already prescribed base simplex. Thus these pullbacks are also trivial fibrations by the same characterization.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.6, expanded into boundary lifting using the anodyne pushout-product; Kan-Quillen boundary characterization from the cited DAG node.

proof.text: Suppose first that $u:U\to W$ is a Kan fibration. Set $E_R=T\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,W,v}V$, let $q_R:E_R\to V$ be projection, and let $a_R:E_R\to W$ be $\operatorname{ev}_0$ on its path coordinate. Step 2 makes $q_R$ a trivial fibration. The constant-path map $s_R:V\to E_R$, $y\mapsto(c_{v(y)},y)$, is simplicial because the constant path is precomposition with $I\to\Delta^0$; it satisfies $q_Rs_R=1_V$ and $a_Rs_R=v$ in every degree. The model structure asserted by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] has the two-out-of-three axiom, so $q_R$ being a weak equivalence and $q_Rs_R=1$ imply that $s_R$ is a weak equivalence. By the degreewise pullback definition, $P(u,v)=U\times_{W,u,a_R}E_R$ and its projection $r_R:P(u,v)\to E_R$ is a Kan fibration: given a horn problem, project it to the horn problem for $u$, lift there, and pair that lift with the prescribed simplex of $E_R$. The pullback of $s_R$ along $r_R$ is canonically $U\times_W V$: a simplex in this pullback has path exactly $c_{v(y)}$ and satisfies $u(x)=v(y)$. Its map to $P(u,v)$ is consequently exactly $(x,y)\mapsto(x,c_{u(x)},y)$. Right properness in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], applied to the weak equivalence $s_R$ and the Kan fibration $r_R$, proves that this particular constant-path comparison is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7, proof with f_0 a Kan fibration; its application of Proposition 3.4.0.2 (0109) is implemented by the existing right-properness statement.

proof.text: If instead $v:V\to W$ is a Kan fibration, use $E_L=U\times_{u,W,\operatorname{ev}_0}T$, with projection $q_L:E_L\to U$ and $a_L:E_L\to W$ given by $\operatorname{ev}_1$. Step 2 makes $q_L$ a trivial fibration, and $s_L:U\to E_L$, $x\mapsto(x,c_{u(x)})$, satisfies $q_Ls_L=1_U$ and $a_Ls_L=u$. Two-out-of-three in the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] again makes $s_L$ a weak equivalence. Now $P(u,v)=E_L\times_{a_L,W,v}V$, and $r_L:P(u,v)\to E_L$ is a Kan fibration by projecting each horn problem to $v$ and pairing its filler with the prescribed simplex of $E_L$. The pullback of $s_L$ along $r_L$ consists in each degree of $x,y$ with $u(x)=v(y)$ and path exactly $c_{u(x)}$. Therefore its map to $P(u,v)$ is the stated comparison from $U\times_W V$. Right properness applied to $s_L$ and $r_L$ proves the required weak equivalence. This argument treats the second endpoint directly and uses no reversal of the simplicial interval.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7, the other fibration case; endpoint 0 version of the preceding construction, written explicitly.

lean.statement: theorem kan_pullback_path_comparison {U V W : SSet.{u}} [KanComplex U] [KanComplex V] [KanComplex W] (u : U ⟶ W) (v : V ⟶ W) : ∃ c : pullback u v ⟶ pullback (pullback.snd u (evaluation Δ[1] W (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 0)) ≫ evaluation Δ[1] W (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 1)) v, c ≫ pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst u v ∧ c ≫ pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.fst u v ≫ u ≫ constantDiagrams Δ[1] W ∧ c ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd u v ∧ KanComplex (pullback (pullback.snd u (evaluation Δ[1] W (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 0)) ≫ evaluation Δ[1] W (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 1)) v) ∧ ((Fibration u ∨ Fibration v) → IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence c)
lean.note: The three projection equations uniquely specify the constant-path comparison; the Kan assertion precedes the conditional weak-equivalence assertion. All constructions use the recorded enhanced-diagram primitives and Mathlib pullbacks.
